updates.name: William P. Bowman
updates.bio: Retired (June 2021) University of Colorado Boulder plant ecologist. The Bowman lab examined how alpine plants interact with soil resources, including limits on primary production, competition and facilitation, symbiotic nitrogen fixation and plant effects on nitrogen cycling, work used to predict nitrogen deposition impacts and to inform mountain air quality standards in the western U.S. and central Europe.
updates.research_interests: plant ecology; terrestrial ecosystem science; nutrient relations of alpine plants; resource use in plant communities; controls on alpine primary production and nutrient fluxes; competition and facilitation among plants
updates.current_title: Professor Emeritus, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
updates.evidence: Professor Bowman retired in June 2021 and is no longer carrying out research or teaching.
updates.notes: EBIO profile (200) lists 'Professor Emeritus, EBIO' with research interests and links the lab site www.colorado.edu/bowmanlab/ (200), which states the June 2021 retirement. ORCID 0000-0003-0158-4039: pub.orcid.org person record name 'WILLIAM BOWMAN', employment University of Colorado Boulder (no department given); its works (alpine sedge responses to nitrogen deposition 2019; limited ecosystem recovery from simulated chronic N deposition 2018; stochasticity and biotic interactions in alpine plant patterning 2018) match the EBIO profile's selected publications. Neither page links Google Scholar. Neither page mentions Rocky Mountain National Park; the ROMO collaborator row was not re-checked here.

updates.name: Keith Laakkonen
updates.bio: Sanctuary Director of the National Audubon Society's Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary in Naples, Florida, appointed in January 2023. Before that, as a Florida Department of Environmental Protection employee, he directed Rookery Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, overseeing 110,000 acres, and served as National Estuarine Research Reserve Association president. His interests include watershed management, wildlife ecology, prescribed fire and hydrologic restoration.
updates.research_interests: watershed restoration and management; managing species and wildlife ecology; prescribed burning; restoring hydrology; exotic plant and animal control; environmental education and outreach
updates.evidence: most recently worked for the Florida Department of Environmental Protection as Director at Rookery Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve in Naples
updates.notes: VERIFIER: the earlier bio called him current Rookery Bay director and NERRA president 'in 2025', from a Rookery Bay news post that its page dates June 2, 2025 (a repost date). Audubon Florida's announcement of January 9, 2023 (200) says Audubon named him Director of Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary and that he most recently was Director at Rookery Bay NERR for Florida DEP and had been NERRA president; his Audubon people page (https://www.audubon.org/people/keith-laakkonen, 200) still lists him as Sanctuary Director. updates.name: Tim Brown
updates.bio: Director of both Sagehen Creek Field Station and Chickering American River Reserve, UC Nature reserves on opposite slopes of the Sierra Nevada. In 2025 Brown expected to finish a doctorate in ecology and evolutionary biology at UC Santa Cruz and announced a new Sagehen grant for UC graduate field research that adds support for mentoring undergraduates.

updates.name: Katharyn Boyer
updates.bio: San Francisco State University biology professor since 2004 and interim executive director of its Estuary & Ocean Science Center. A coastal ecologist working chiefly in salt marshes and seagrass beds, Boyer studies how species shape habitats and ecosystem processes and applies that to restoration, leading living-shoreline projects that restore eelgrass and native oysters and test their shore-protection value.
updates.research_interests: coastal wetland restoration; community ecology; biodiversity effects on ecosystem function; nutrient dynamics; food-web interactions; habitat structure; living shorelines
updates.current_title: Professor; Interim Executive Director, Estuary & Ocean Science Center
updates.evidence: Katharyn Boyer Professor; Interim Executive Director, EOS Center

updates.name: Margot Buchbinder
updates.bio: Lead technician and lab manager of the Boyer Lab since 2018. Runs the lab's daily operations, manages several living-shoreline projects and studies on eelgrass, California sea-blite and cordgrass ecology and restoration, and helps lab members with R programming.

updates.name: Anna Deck
updates.bio: Lead research technician with San Francisco Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, coordinating System-Wide Monitoring Program work and its data and contributing to other Bay research. Holds UC Davis ecology degrees (B.S., M.Sc.); thesis research at Bodega Marine Laboratory examined native bivalves along estuarine gradients. Has since studied invertebrates, fish and water quality in several California estuaries, favouring management-relevant research.
updates.research_interests: estuarine invertebrate and fish communities; water quality; management-relevant ecological research
updates.current_affiliation: San Francisco Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (San Francisco State University)
updates.evidence: Anna focuses on coordination and data management for the System-Wide Monitoring Program
updates.notes: SF Bay NERR People page (200) carries a staff bio paragraph; staff who have left are marked '(former)' there and she is not, hence status active.
